security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline API formatting, placeholder Azure URLs, and normal SDK configuration examples. The main remaining concern is semantic: the skill demonstrates destructive Azure Container Registry operations that require confirmation, dry-run checks, and careful scoping.

remediation.issue: Destructive Azure Container Registry examples lack explicit safety gates.
remediation.suggestion: Add dry-run examples, require explicit user confirmation, and scope deletes by registry, repository, tag, and digest before calling delete methods.

remediation.issue: Blob download example writes to a fixed local archive name.
remediation.suggestion: Document that output paths should be user-approved, local to the workspace, and checked before overwriting existing files.

content.user_title: Manage Azure Container Registry with Python
content.value_statement: Azure Container Registry work often requires precise SDK calls for repositories, tags, manifests, and blobs. This skill gives Python examples for authentication, listing, updates, deletion, downloads, and async clients.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install and import azure-containerregistry.
Lists repositories, tags, and manifest metadata.
Updates repository and manifest write or delete properties.
Deletes repositories, tags, manifests, and old untagged images.
Downloads manifests and layer blobs, including async client usage.
limitations: Does not provide a runnable application or tests.
Requires Azure credentials and registry permissions before examples work.
Deletion examples can remove registry artifacts if used on production resources.
Does not cover container image push or build workflows.

use_cases.title: Inventory Registry Content
use_cases.description: List repositories, tags, and manifests to understand what images exist in an Azure Container Registry.

use_cases.title: Build Python Registry Tools
use_cases.description: Use SDK examples to create scripts that inspect registry metadata and download artifacts.

use_cases.title: Control Image Lifecycle
use_cases.description: Lock important images and plan cleanup for old untagged manifests with clear safeguards.

prompt_templates.title: List Registry Repositories
prompt_templates.prompt: Use azure-containerregistry-py to show a basic Python example that authenticates with DefaultAzureCredential and lists repositories in my Azure Container Registry.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Image Metadata
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to write Python steps for reading tags and manifests for <repository>. Include sorting by most recent update.

prompt_templates.title: Protect Production Images
prompt_templates.prompt: Use azure-containerregistry-py to draft a Python snippet that disables delete and write operations for a production repository and manifest.

prompt_templates.title: Design Cleanup Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use azure-containerregistry-py to design a safe cleanup process for untagged manifests older than 30 days. Include dry-run output, confirmation, and async considerations.

output_examples.input: List every repository in my registry.
output_examples.output: A short Python workflow that authenticates with DefaultAzureCredential, creates a ContainerRegistryClient, iterates repository names, and reminds you to set the registry endpoint.

output_examples.input: Find old untagged manifests before cleanup.
output_examples.output: A cleanup plan that compares manifest update dates to a cutoff, prints candidates first, and deletes only after explicit approval.

output_examples.input: Download a layer blob for inspection.
output_examples.output: A download workflow that retrieves the blob by digest, writes it to a named archive, and advises using a safe local path.

best_practices: Use Entra ID and least privilege roles for registry automation.
Run destructive operations in dry-run mode before deleting artifacts.
Prefer digest-based cleanup and verify tags before deletion.
anti_patterns: Do not run delete examples against production registries without explicit confirmation.
Do not hardcode credentials or registry secrets in scripts.
Do not assume a tag uniquely identifies the content you intend to delete.

faq.question: What Azure service does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Azure Container Registry through the azure-containerregistry Python SDK.

faq.question: Does it support authenticated registries?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples use DefaultAzureCredential for Entra ID authentication.

faq.question: Can it work with public registries?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an anonymous client example for Microsoft Container Registry.

faq.question: Can it delete registry content?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes delete examples, so users should require confirmation and dry-run checks.

faq.question: Does it include async usage?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill shows the async ContainerRegistryClient and credential cleanup.

faq.question: Does it build or push container images?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on registry metadata, artifacts, downloads, and lifecycle operations.
